memos.scout:
The honest case for buying SXI is weak, and I'd recommend skipping it.

What the brief shows in its favor: the coin is alive at 30 minutes, it's up 135% over that window, and the last 15 minutes carried real volume (about $71k, 1,721 buyers, 294 SOL bought). Net flow over that stretch was slightly negative (-15.7 SOL), so buying was roughly matched by selling rather than overwhelmed by it.

The case against is stronger. The curve shows bundle_share of 1.0, meaning every early buy came through bundled transactions, and the completer and top-3 shares are high (83% and 85%), suggesting a few wallets drove the move. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.76, and the coin is already 30% off its 30-minute high with a 27% loss over the last 15 minutes. Buyers are arriving, but sellers are keeping pace and momentum is fading. Against a base rate of about -20% for random buys in this window, and with round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% on top, nothing here argues that demand will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss is a dip-and-bleed after a sharp fall from the peak. SXI is down 30% from its 30-minute high and -26.8% over the last 15 minutes, with net flow of -15.66 SOL: sells (309.74 SOL) outran buys (294.08 SOL). The sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.76, and 461 sellers now versus 1,721 buyers suggests early holders are unwinding. The curve data is concerning: bundle_share is 1.0 and the top 3 wallets hold 84.8% of the curve, so a single cluster can exit against retail. With a 132.9 SOL pool, a $20 ticket faces 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs, and a further 5-10% drift eats any bounce. The 1.35x return over 30 minutes is a stale signal already reversing. Skip.
